To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we have developed a simple method for generating images from a word embedding, (b) the generated images are sufficient to discriminate among general categories of objects, and (c) we have shown that the method can be used for image generation in a variety of domains, such as animals, food, and vehicles.

1) the proposed method is a simple yet effective approach to language-driven image generation; 2) the images produced by the system capture general visual properties, such as typical environment or color, of the concepts encoded by the word embedding; 3) the images produced are sufficient to discriminate general categories of objects; 4) the method is robust to the choice of word embedding and visual space; and 5) the method can be used as a tool to explore the contents of word embedding

(i) it is feasible to use word embeddings to generate natural images of concepts; (ii) the images generated by our simple method can be used to discriminate between different concepts; (iii) the generated images capture general visual properties (color, typical environment); (iv) the generated images are more similar to the ground truth image than the images generated by a simple baseline method; (v) our system outperforms state-of-the-art systems for language-driven image generation in a user study;
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) Can a simple method based only on word embeddings generate images that capture the semantic contents of the words? (ii) How well do these generated images capture the visual properties of the words?

the following questions. Can word embeddings be used to generate images? If so, how can we do it? What is the quality of the resulting images? What are the implications of such a task for the field of image synthesis?
the following question: given the word embedding for a concept, can we generate images that capture the general properties of the concept?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current system does not generate images of the objects that are encoded in the word embeddings, but rather it generates images of the general visual properties of these objects.

the system is not able to generate an image that captures the full meaning of a concept, but is able to generate images that are consistent with the semantic information encoded by a given word embedding.
our method can generate images that are visually appealing and capture the semantics of a word embedding to some extent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that word embeddings contain visual information that can be extracted using simple mapping functions and that the resulting images can be used to visualize the visual information contained in word embeddings.
our method is able to generate a visual representation that captures the semantic content of a word embedding.
we have developed a method for generating images that are semantically consistent with word embeddings and that can be used to visualize word embeddings in an intuitive way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, even with a very simple method, word embeddings can be used as a bridge to generate images of concepts, which opens up the possibility to use word embedding models for a variety of tasks that involve visualizing the semantic content of a word, such as image retrieval or image captioning.
, even though word embeddings are often considered a black box and used as a proxy to represent semantic knowledge, they can actually be interpreted in visual space.
the visual properties encoded in word embeddings can be visualized in natural images, which suggests that word embeddings are a promising source for image generation.
